summary: Session token rotation interferes with pin coherence during incremental canary causing cross-variant fallbacks
description:
Issue summary:
During an incremental canary rollout for redwood-open-7b-v2 in us-west, the customer (BrightAssist AI) reported a rise in cross-variant fallback responses where traffic pinned to the new canary model intermittently routed to an older model. This coincided with our recent session-token rotation job running during the same maintenance window.

Impact:
- ~2% of requests from a subset of pinned sessions returned responses from the fallback model (open-llama-7b-q4_0) instead of the pinned canary.
- Customer reports degraded QA metrics for conversation continuity and higher token costs.
- Incident impacted a single dedicated region (us-west) and affected several long-running user sessions.

Environment:
- Dedicated deployment (BrightAssist AI) on prod us-west
- Serving runtime: v3.8.1
- Edge/session proxy: session-proxy v1.14
- Canary rollout: incremental (10% -> 25%) over 2026-03-10 02:00-04:00 UTC

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Start canary rollout for redwood-open-7b-v2 with session-affinity preserved.
2) Trigger session-token rotation job (automated security task that rotates session tokens/leases).
3) Long-running sessions that received a pinned token experienced token refresh mid-stream.
4) Some edge nodes rejected rotated token headers causing a re-authorization path that did not carry the pin metadata.
5) Requests without pin metadata were routed by policy to the fallback (older) model under burst constraints.

Observed behavior:
- Intermittent 200 responses that contained outputs inconsistent with the canary variant (style/stop-words matched older model).
- No 5xx errors; routing decision led to expected but unwanted variant responses.
- Session logs show header rewrite/drop on specific edge-proxy instances.

Expected behavior:
- Session-token rotation should preserve pin-coherence: rotated tokens must retain or re-associate the session-level pin metadata so requests remain pinned to the intended model variant.

Attachments/Logs:
- tail of session-proxy logs (errors showing header validation mismatches) attached in ticket thread.
- Route coordinator traces showing decision tree for sample session IDs.
- Customer provided transcripts highlighting semantic divergence.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Maya Chen (Support): Initial report and customer transcript received. Marking P1 due to production QA impact. Notifying SRE on-call.
2026-03-10 - SRE on-call (Arjun Patel): Reproduced header drop on edge-proxy instance ep-12. Suspect token rotation handshake timing race. Captured pcap and traces.

2026-03-11 - Routing eng (Lars Becker): Confirmed some requests lost pin metadata after token refresh; edge-proxy returned 200 but omitted x-session-pin header before proxy->coordinator hop. Investigating why proxy didn't reattach pin after reauth.

2026-03-12 - Session proxy eng (Nina Alvarez): Found a bug in session-proxy v1.14 where rotated-token code path mistakenly clears temporary metadata when auth returns 204 (no-body). Preparing hotfix branch.

2026-03-12 - Customer (BrightAssist AI - ops): Confirmed symptom window matches their internal maintenance window. They've applied a temporary mitigation (pause canary expansion) and requested ETA for fix.
2026-03-13 - Support (Maya Chen): Escalated to PM for coordination on patch rollout and asked customer if they can accept a staged patch on their dedicated nodes tonight.

2026-03-13 - Engineering (Lars Becker): Hotfix PR opened and smoke tests green in staging. Planning a targeted restart of session-proxy fleet in us-west for 2026-03-13 22:00 UTC. Scheduled rollback if regressions observed.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: session-token rotation handshake returns a 204 (no-content) path that clears ephemeral headers; session-proxy code treats 204 as success and does not rehydrate pin metadata.

Hypothesis 2: route-coordinator relies on x-session-pin header strictly from edge; if header absent, it applies fallback policies even when a server-side session store contains pin data. Some requests short-circuited coordinator lookup due to cache TTL mismatch.

Evidence: packet traces show auth response sequence where rotated token accepted but edge-proxy emitted downstream request without x-session-pin for ~15s window on ep-12 and ep-17. Route coordinator logs show fallback path invoked for those requests.
Repro steps validated in staging by invoking rotation job concurrently with simulated canary traffic; saw identical header loss on session-proxy image with v1.14 but not on v1.13.
Scope estimate: ~2-3% of active pinned sessions in rollout cohort experienced at least one fallback call in the observed window. No data loss or secret exposure observed.
Risk assessment: fix is low-risk code change to session-proxy rehydrate path but requires coordinated restart of edge nodes to pick up fix in dedicated customer environment.
resolution_notes: Workaround (customer applied): Pause canary expansion and instruct client to reconnect affected sessions to force rebind; this immediately reduced cross-variant fallbacks to <0.1%.

Fix deployed: session-proxy hotfix v1.14.1 released that preserves and reattaches x-session-pin after token rotation when auth returns 204. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/session-proxy/pull/331
Rollout plan: staged restart of us-west session-proxy instances in waves of 5% to limit interruption. Completed 2026-03-13 23:15 UTC. Smoke tests and customer validation passed.
Verification: Post-deploy traces show no header loss during rotation; monitored pinned-variant hit-rate for cohort improved from ~98% to >99.9% within 30 minutes.

Follow-ups: (1) Add an end-to-end test for token rotation + pin preservation in our canary harness. (2) Update runbook to avoid running token rotation jobs during canary expansions for dedicated customers until automated canary-friendly rotation is implemented. (3) Add observability metric for x-session-pin drops at edge-proxy.
Communication: Notified customer of fix and closure steps; recommended resuming canary expansion after confirmation window. Ticket to be closed after 48h of stable metrics.
